<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 50.0pt;text-indent:-50.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 1.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.5pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Business</b><a name="Item1_Business_143917"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Introduction</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company was
incorporated in Utah in 1974 as Motion Control, Inc.&#160; In 1987, the Company merged with JMW
Acquisition Corporation, and the name of the merged entity was changed to
IOMED, Inc.&#160; We are a leader in
developing, manufacturing and marketing active drug delivery systems used
primarily to treat acute local inflammation in the physical and occupational
therapy and sports medicine markets.&#160; We
are pursuing opportunities to advance our position as a provider of quality,
innovative medical products that improve patient healthcare.&#160; In addition, we are seeking collaborative
opportunities to develop our non-invasive drug delivery technology to satisfy
unmet medical needs.&#160; We have proprietary
iontophoresis technology in various stages of research and product development
for transdermal drug delivery and for the treatment of ophthalmic disease.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Strategic Assessment Update</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On September 15,
2005, we announced that our Board of Directors decided to explore various
strategic alternatives for the Company to maximize shareholder value.&#160; In connection with this process, we retained
Seven Hills Partners LLC to act as our financial advisor.&#160; We are engaged in discussions with various
parties regarding potential transactions.&#160;
At the present time, the assessment of strategic alternatives is
ongoing.&#160; We are uncertain whether any
transaction will result from this process and if a transaction does result from
that process what form it will take.</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Commercial Business</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are in the
business of developing, manufacturing, and marketing proprietary products used
in the site-specific, non-invasive administration of soluble salts or other
drugs into the body for medical purposes.&#160;
Our active drug delivery systems employ iontophoresis (explained more
fully below) as a non-invasive method of enhancing and controlling the
transport of water-soluble ionic drugs into and through the skin and other body
tissues using a low-level electrical current.&#160;
We currently market iontophoretic products used to deliver various drug
compounds.&#160; The primary drug compounds
currently used with our products are potent corticosteroids for the treatment
of acute local inflammatory conditions.&#160;
In addition,</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">3</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='3',FILE='C:\Jms\nnarend\06-20304-1\task1385755\20304-1-fa.htm',USER='nnarayanan',CD='Sep 27 19:54 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Iontocaine</font><font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>, our brand of lidocaine HCl 2%
and epinephrine 1:100,000 topical solution, has been approved by the Food and
Drug Administration (&#147;FDA&#148;) under a New Drug Application (&#147;NDA&#148;) for the
administration of local dermal anesthesia, but is not currently marketed.&#160; Our products are used in situations when it
is advisable to avoid the pain that may accompany needle insertion and drug
injection, to minimize the infiltration of carrier fluids, and/or to avoid the
damage caused by needle insertion when tissue is traumatized.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="191" height="200" src="g203041fai001.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our proprietary,
patented iontophoresis system (the &#147;Phoresor</font><font face="Symbol">&#226;</font>
system&#148; or &#147;Phoresor&#148;) is designed for clinical use and is comprised of a
reusable dose controller and single use, disposable active transdermal patch
kits (&#147;patch kits&#148;).&#160; The dose controller
incorporates an advanced microprocessor to precisely control drug dosage
through our proprietary single-use, disposable patch kits, including our IOGEL<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#174;</font>, TransQ<font size="1" face="Symbol" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#226;</font>, and OptimA<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#153;</font>&#160;patch kits.&#160; We also market a self-contained iontophoresis
system, the Companion 80<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#153;</font>, that
provides a Mobile Solution<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">&#153;</font>&#160;allowing the patient to resume daily activity
and the clinician to optimize the use of patient time in the clinic.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="197" height="129" src="g203041fai002.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Using our products,
medical professionals are able to deliver dexamethasone, a potent and effective
corticosteroid, to treat local inflammatory conditions.&#160; Our proprietary products, combined with
dexamethasone, have the potential to address a significant unmet medical need
by offering patients the benefits of the anti-inflammatory effects of
dexamethasone while avoiding all of the gastrointestinal (GI) and other
systemic side effects of oral drugs, such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory
drugs (NSAIDs), including Cox-II inhibitors.&#160;
Because of the negative side effects often associated with the oral or
injectable administration of corticosteroids, dexamethasone is used only as a
second- or third-line therapy.&#160; However,
using our technology, the administration of this drug without the occurrence of
these negative side effects is possible.&#160;
Our products are used for site-specific corticosteroid therapy in
clinics nationwide to treat a variety of conditions, including those suffered
by top professional, collegiate, and Olympic athletes.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="575" height="241" src="g203041fai003.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our products are
also used by clinicians to deliver a wide-range of other water-soluble ionic
medicaments for treatment of a variety of conditions.&#160; These conditions include providing
non-invasive, local dermal anesthesia with rapid onset that can be used prior
to needle sticks, IV starts, lumbar punctures, PICC insertions, fine needle and
skin biopsies, and other minor dermatological surgeries.</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Business Strategy</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The majority of
our revenues are generated through the sale of the Phoresor system, which
consists of a reusable dose controller and single-use disposable patch
kits.&#160; We are continuously seeking
opportunities to improve the quality of our existing products and to market or
develop new products to support this &#147;razor-razor blade&#148; business model.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We intend to
promote growth in our core business by:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Strengthen Product Lines </i>&#150; Leverage
existing distributor networks and health care provider relationships and enter
into new agreements to broaden and strengthen access to our served markets.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Develop New Products </i>&#150; Apply technological
expertise on focused product development activities to provide value to our
customers and to improve the competitive position of our products and our
distributors.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><i>Seek New Product and Market Opportunities</i> &#150;Expand
product offerings, identify new products and enter new markets both
independently and through acquisition or collaborative relationships.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Acute
Local Inflammation</font></i></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="467" height="516" src="g203041fai004.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Acute local
inflammatory conditions resulting from exercise, sports injuries, trauma or
repetitive motion disorders are among the leading types of injuries occurring
in the workplace and among physically active adults.&#160; The most common of these injuries include
tendonitis, bursitis, carpal tunnel syndrome and epicondylitis (tennis
elbow).&#160; We believe the electro-transport
of corticosteroids may provide significant advantages over other current treatment
regimens for acute local inflammation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Commercial
Products</font></i>.&#160; We pioneered
the commercial introduction of our active transdermal drug delivery systems in
1979.&#160; These products are used
principally by physical therapists (under a doctor&#146;s prescription) and have
been clinically administered in over 28 million patient treatments for the
delivery of corticosteroids and other drugs.&#160;
More than 26 million of these treatments have occurred since 1990, when
advancements we made in our patch technology led to the introduction of our
present range of hydrogel patches for use with our microprocessor controlled
dose controllers.&#160; Our products are also
used by athletic trainers and physical therapists serving a number of professional,
collegiate, and Olympic athletes and teams, including golfers, tennis players,
men&#146;s and women&#146;s Olympic ski teams, as well as by football, basketball,
baseball and hockey teams.&#160; We believe
that our active transdermal drug delivery systems have been accepted in the
rehabilitation marketplace due to their ease of use, non-invasiveness,
recognized efficacy and lack of significant side effects.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="200" height="187" src="g203041fai005.jpg"></font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">6</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='6',FILE='C:\Jms\nnarend\06-20304-1\task1385755\20304-1-fa.htm',USER='nnarayanan',CD='Sep 27 19:54 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Products
Under Development</font></i>.&#160; We
continue to seek to develop and market &#147;next generation&#148; products for use in
treating acute local inflammatory conditions.&#160;
Enhancements to our dose controllers and electrode patches, as well as
the developing, manufacturing, and marketing of new products are part of our
efforts to provide customers the most advanced iontophoresis technology
commercially available.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="288" height="179" src="g203041fai006.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">IontoDex</font><font face="Symbol">&#228;</font>
is a miniaturized, integrated version of our active drug transport system
designed for patient in-home use to treat acute local inflammation.&#160; This proprietary active drug transport
system, combined with dexamethasone, has the potential to address a significant
unmet medical need by offering patients the benefits of the anti-inflammatory
effects of dexamethasone while avoiding all of the gastrointestinal (GI) and
other systemic side effects of oral drugs, such as non-steroidal anti-inflammatory
drugs (NSAIDs), including Cox-II inhibitors.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal
2001, we completed both a pivotal Phase III and a confirmatory Phase III
clinical study for the delivery of dexamethasone to treat acute local
inflammation.&#160; The confirmatory study
failed to meet primary clinical endpoints.&#160;
The study showed a positive response in patients treated with the drug;
however, increased benefit in the study&#146;s placebo group prevented the
statistical separation between the two patient groups necessary to achieve the
desired conclusions.&#160; Due to these study
results and to financial and other resource constraints, we suspended all major
internal development efforts and may seek corporate development partners or
other strategic funding sources prior to any substantial continuation of this
development program.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Dermal
Anesthesia</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Healthcare
professionals recognize the importance of managing pain associated with
invasive medical procedures, such as needle injections, placement of access
devices (including phlebotomies, IV catheters, lumbar punctures, epidurals,
etc), dermatological procedures (biopsies, wart and mole removal, Mohs
procedures, etc), as well as gynecological and urological procedures
(vasectomies, etc).&#160; In 2001, two new
standards were instituted that are relevant to our product offerings.&#160; The Occupational Safety and Health
Administration (OSHA) revised their Bloodborne Pathogen Standard, requiring
employers to use safer medical devices wherever feasible in order to reduce the
risk of injury from sharps.&#160; The Joint Commission
on Accredited Healthcare Organizations (JCAHO) also passed their new Pain
Management Standards requiring healthcare professionals to inform patients of
methods available to minimize pain prior to, during, and after medical
procedures.&#160; These two standards favor
the type of non-invasive drug delivery systems that we offer and certain
product modifications under consideration could enhance the use of our products
in the dermal anesthesia market.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Commercial
Products</font></i>.&#160; We received
approval by the FDA under a NDA for Iontocaine, which is specifically labeled
for use with our Phoresor system and our proprietary, single use, disposable
active transdermal patch kits.&#160; However,
we do not currently sell Iontocaine due to low historical revenues generated from
product sales relative to product costs and FDA fees.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our products are
currently sold into the pediatric, adult vascular access, and dermatology
markets for use in inducing dermal anesthesia prior to invasive procedures and
for use in other applications.&#160; We
believe our products are more effective than the leading topical product.&#160; However, to date, revenues generated from
these markets have not been significant.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Ophthalmic Diseases</font></i></b></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="437" height="292" src="g203041fai007.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We believe that our unique active drug transport
system presents a significant opportunity in the ophthalmic pharmaceutical
marketplace due to large patient populations with sight threatening medical
needs that are unmet.&#160; Age-related
macular degeneration (&#147;AMD&#148;) and diabetic retinopathy (&#147;DR&#148;) are the major
causes of visual impairment in the United States and Europe. Both AMD and DR
are conditions caused by angiogenesis (unwanted blood vessel growth) resulting
in neovascularization that damages the retina and ultimately causes
blindness.&#160; Posterior uveitis and
retinitis secondary to glaucoma also contribute considerably to loss of sight
worldwide.&#160; A common characteristic among
all of these conditions is their occurrence at the back of the eye, where drug
treatment is difficult to administer.&#160; We
believe that our proprietary drug delivery technology may offer a significant
improvement to the current treatments available and for unmet medical needs in
this area.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A leading obstacle
in the advancement of new therapies to treat serious ophthalmic disease is the
inability to both safely and effectively deliver drugs to diseased cells in the
back of the eye.&#160; Current drug delivery
methods, which include intravenous, oral, topical (eye drops), intraocular
injections and surgical implants, all have limitations that potentially affect their
technical as well as their commercial viability in the treatment of these
diseases.&#160; Furthermore, the complex
physiology of the human eye presents unique problems for drug delivery, which
are not optimally addressed by current ocular drug delivery methods.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="167" height="200" src="g203041fai008.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Development
Stage Products.&#160; </font></i>Using
our proprietary technology, we have developed an ocular drug delivery system
that seeks to address the safe and effective administration of therapeutics to
the back of the eye. Our delivery system, trademarked OcuPhor<font face="Symbol">&#228;</font>,
allows for the site-specific administration of a pharmacologic agent without
the collateral tissue damage associated with surgery, lasers, needle injections
or implants.&#160; OcuPhor has been designed
as a platform technology to deliver drug compounds non-invasively and
site-specifically to posterior segments of the eye.&#160; Through both collaborations and internal
research efforts, we have made significant advancements with the OcuPhor
System.&#160; Feasibility studies confirmed
OcuPhor&#146;s ability to deliver an anti-angiogenic drug to the back of the eye.
Preliminary clinical studies in human volunteers have shown that the OcuPhor
System is safe and well tolerated using both positive and negative polarity
currents and does not produce any ophthalmic changes as measured by a series of
standard tests.&#160; Additionally, we
demonstrated <i>in-vivo </i>that the
OcuPhor System is capable of delivering antiangiogenic, anti-inflammatory,
antibiotic, and antiviral drugs.&#160; We
believe that OcuPhor&#146;s transport capabilities are within the theoretical
therapeutic range of a variety of drugs, including small molecules as well as
some macromolecules and small proteins.&#160;
We are evaluating strategies to capitalize on this technology, including
license agreements and collaborative partnerships to identify specific drugs
which will be able to take advantage of the OcuPhor System and thereafter move
it beyond the preclinical stage and advance its commercial development.</p>

<h3 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">General Iontophoretic Drug Delivery Technology and Its
Advantages</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Iontophoretic drug
delivery systems are designed to overcome many of the limitations associated
with other drug delivery methods.&#160;
Iontophoresis is an active method of drug delivery in which
water-soluble, ionized (electrically charged) drugs are transported through the
skin or other body tissues for local or systemic therapeutic applications by
applying a low-level electrical current.&#160;
The amount of drug delivered is proportional to the total electrical
charge applied (which is a function of time and current).&#160; Therefore, it is possible to program the
system&#146;s electrical current levels to control more precisely the desired drug
dose, delivery rate and the pattern of delivery.</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><img width="590" height="253" src="g203041fai010.jpg"></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Among the many
drug delivery methods available today, we believe the advantages of iontophoretic
drug delivery are many and include the following:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Non-invasive, needle-free</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Site-specific drug delivery
eliminates systemic side effects</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Rapid onset and cessation kinetics</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Controlled, programmable and
titratable drug delivery capabilities</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Single delivery system provides
smooth, variable or bolus plasma levels, singly or in combination</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Enhanced delivery of a broad range of
compounds</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Minimal variability in the delivery
profiles among patients and body sites</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Potential for enhanced patient
compliance and control</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Meets OSHA pain management standards
for healthcare industry</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 36.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>Compliance
with Needle Stick Prevention Act of 2001.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although the
fundamentals of iontophoresis have been understood for decades, the method only
became commercially practicable as a means of delivering drugs as a result of
advances in electronics, materials science and electrochemistry.&#160; These advances led to the development of more
efficient and adaptable drug patches and more reliable, compact and
programmable dose controllers.&#160; We have
used our portfolio of intellectual property to develop iontophoretic systems
with unique and enhanced performance characteristics, which we believe are
adaptable to a number of clinical settings and therapeutic applications.</font></p>

and Proprietary Rights</font></b></p>

various combinations in the testing, evaluation and formulation of optimal
ionic drug solutions and in the research, development, design and manufacture

which are specifically designed and constructed for particular therapeutic
applications.</font></p>

We also rely on trade secrets, know-how, continuous technological
innovations and licensing opportunities to develop and maintain a competitive
position.&#160; We seek protection of our
trade secrets and</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Government
Regulation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Both drugs and
medical devices, including our iontophoretic drug delivery systems, are subject
to extensive regulation by the FDA in the United States and by comparable
authorities in other foreign countries.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our iontophoretic
drug delivery products involve a medical device component, thereby subjecting
such products to compliance with the FDA&#146;s regulations governing medical
devices.&#160; Where such medical devices are
labeled for use with a specific pharmaceutical product for a specific
therapeutic indication, they are subject to the FDA&#146;s regulations governing
both medical devices and pharmaceutical products.&#160; The Company&#146;s future iontophoretic drug
delivery systems may involve a pharmaceutical component or specific labeling
for use with a pharmaceutical product.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">11</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='11',FILE='C:\Jms\nnarend\06-20304-1\task1385755\20304-1-fa.htm',USER='nnarayanan',CD='Sep 27 19:54 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Products regulated
as medical devices may not be commercially distributed in the United States
unless they have been cleared or approved by the FDA.&#160; Currently, there are two methods for
obtaining FDA clearance or approval of medical devices.&#160; Devices deemed to pose less risk are placed
in class I (general controls) or class II (general and special controls) and
qualify for 510(k) notification, a procedure under section 510(k) of the
Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act.&#160; A
medical device that does not qualify for the 510(k) clearance is placed in
class III, which is reserved for devices deemed by the FDA to pose the greatest
risk. A preamendment class III device is one that was on the market before May
28, 1976.&#160; This status means that the
device at present can be marketed through a 510(k) clearance, but it remains
subject to a call for a Pre-Market Approval (&#147;PMA&#148;) application under section
515 of the Drug Act.&#160; A PMA application
generally requires a more complex submission than a 510(k) notification.&#160; Typically, it requires showing that the
device is safe and effective based on extensive and costly preclinical and
clinical tests, as well as information about the device and its components
regarding, among other things, manufacturing, labeling and promotion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The regulatory
status of iontophoretic devices is complex.&#160;
The FDA has classified them as class II devices eligible for marketing
through 510(k) premarket clearance when intended for use with a drug whose
labeling bears adequate directions for the device&#146;s use with that drug.&#160; However, if an iontophoretic device is
intended for use with a drug that is not labeled for use with the device, the
FDA considers the iontophoresis device to be a preamendment class III device.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our Phoresor
received 510(k) clearance as a preamendment class III device labeled for use
with ions of soluble salts or other drugs.&#160;
In 1995, the FDA approved an NDA for Iontocaine to be used as a local
anesthetic and delivered iontophoretically by the Phoresor, which effectively
moved the Phoresor into class II for this intended use.&#160; Unlike Iontocaine, dexamethasone does not have
an NDA approval allowing it to be labeled for iontophoretic delivery.&#160; Thus, at the present time, our Phoresor is a
preamendment class III device when used with dexamethasone (or any drug other
than Iontocaine).&#160; We are not currently
seeking, and give no assurance that we will ever obtain, an approved NDA for
the iontophoretic delivery of any drug other than Iontocaine.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In August 2000,
the FDA published a proposed rule to amend the physical medical device
regulations to remove the class III iontophoresis device identification.&#160; Because our products are all approved as
class II devices, we do not believe that the proposed regulation would have any
effect on our ability to continue the manufacturing and selling of our current
products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A lengthy and
complex regulatory framework also applies to the labeling and marketing of
specific drugs.&#160; Generally these
pharmaceutical products require the submission of an NDA.&#160; The NDA approval process generally entails:
(i) conducting preclinical laboratory and animal testing to enable FDA
authorization of an Investigational New Drug (&#147;IND&#148;) application, (ii) initial
IND clinical studies to define safety and dose parameters, (iii) well
controlled IND clinical trials to demonstrate product safety and efficacy, and
(iv) submission to the FDA of an NDA.&#160;
Preclinical studies involve laboratory evaluation of product
characteristics and animal studies to assess the efficacy and safety of the
drug.&#160; Human clinical trials are
typically conducted in three sequential phases.&#160;
Phase I trials normally consist of testing the product in a small number
of healthy volunteers for safety and pharmacokinetic parameters using single
and multiple dosing regimens.&#160; In Phase
II trials, the manufacturer evaluates safety, initial efficacy, and dose
ranging of the product for specific indications in a somewhat larger patient
population.&#160; Phase III trials typically
involve expanded testing for safety and clinical efficacy in a broad patient
population at multiple clinical testing centers.&#160; The FDA, under Good Laboratory Practice
regulations, regulates the preclinical and clinical studies.&#160; Results of the studies must be submitted to
the FDA for review.&#160; The FDA may grant
marketing approval, require additional testing and/or information, or deny the
application.&#160; The process of obtaining
FDA approval for a new product through this process may take several years and
typically involves substantial risks and the expenditure of substantial
resources.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The FDA regulates
our quality control and manufacturing procedures by requiring us and certain of
our contract suppliers to comply with certain standards, including compliance
with the Quality System Regulations (for devices) and current GMP regulations
(for drugs).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We may be subject
to certain fees that the FDA is authorized to collect, including user fees
authorized under the Public Health Security and Bioterrorism Preparedness and
Response Act of 2002, which include the reauthorization of user fees under the
Prescription Drug User Fee Amendments of 2002 (PDUFA III).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Agencies similar
to the FDA regulate medical devices and pharmaceutical products in most foreign
countries. The International Standards Organization (ISO) has established
regulations for medical devices in the European Union. Currently, we are in
compliance with these regulations and our products are CE Marked. We will be
required to meet the regulations of any foreign country where we market our
products. In addition, various aspects of our business and operations are also
regulated by a number of other governmental agencies, including the Drug
Enforcement Agency, U.S. Department of Agriculture, the Environmental
Protection Agency, the Occupational Safety and Health Administration as well as
by other federal, state and local authorities.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Noncompliance with
these various government regulatory requirements could result in enforcement
actions that could include fines, plant closure, and a recall of our products
or other civil or criminal sanctions. Noncompliance as well as unanticipated
changes in existing regulatory requirements or adoption of new requirements
could have a material adverse effect on the Company.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Competition</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The drug delivery,
pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries are highly competitive and rapidly
evolving, with significant developments expected to continue at a rapid
pace.&#160; Our success depends upon
maintaining a competitive position and developing products and technologies for
efficient and cost effective drug delivery.&#160;
Our products compete with other drugs and drug delivery systems, including
other iontophoretic delivery systems.&#160; We
believe our products compete on the basis of quality, efficacy, cost,
convenience, safety and patient compliance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are aware of
many other competitors in the general field of drug delivery, including, among
others, competitors developing injectable or implantable drug delivery systems,
oral drug delivery technologies, passive transdermal systems, oral transmucosal
systems and intranasal and inhalation systems.&#160;
We are also aware of other companies that have developed or are
currently developing iontophoretic and other active transdermal drug delivery
systems.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Alza, Vyteris,
Inc., Travanti, Inc., and Empi, Inc. are the principal competitors engaged in
the development and/or marketing of iontophoretic devices.&#160; Alza, a licensee of the Company, is
undertaking the development of iontophoretic drug delivery systems, but does
not currently market an iontophoretic product.&#160;
In May 2006, Alza received FDA approval for a combination product, which
employs iontophoresis technology, for the delivery of fentanyl for acute post
operative pain control.&#160; Vyteris is
engaged in the development of iontophoretic drug delivery systems and currently
sells an iontophoretic product for the inducement of dermal anesthesia.&#160; Empi, our primary competitor, and Travanti
currently sell iontophoretic systems for the treatment of acute local
inflammation in the physical therapy market.&#160;
We estimate that Empi controls a majority of that market.&#160; In addition, Encore Medical, the parent
company of Empi, acquired Compex Technologies, a former distributor of ours, in
fiscal 2006 (see further discussion on page 11).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our iontophoretic
system for the inducement of dermal anesthesia primarily competes with
traditional methods of delivering dermal anesthetics by needle injection or is
used in circumstances where either no anesthesia is used, due to the pain
associated with needle injection (including needle injections themselves), or
where topical anesthetic creams are used.&#160;
The most effective and widely used topical anesthetic cream, EMLA, is
manufactured and sold by AstraZeneca International, a large international
pharmaceutical company.&#160; There can be no
assurance that we can effectively compete with these products or any other drug
delivery system.</font></p>

work stoppages and consider our relations with employees to be good.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We
rely on a limited number of independent third party distributors to sell our
products, one of whom recently terminated their distribution agreement with us.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We market our
products through a nationwide network of independent third party distributors
and manufacturing sales representatives, which provide us indirect access to
the clinicians that use our products to administer patient treatments.&#160; Limited access to end user customers may result
in reduced future sales and market penetration of current and future
products.&#160; Our sales growth is dependent
on our ability to broaden distribution and market penetration of our current
and future products, which may require an expanded marketing presence through
direct sales and marketing or co-marketing of products with collaborative
partners or distributors that have national or market-specific marketing
capabilities.&#160; We may not be able to
maintain existing, or establish new, marketing arrangements on favorable terms,
if at all.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Two distributors
combined to account for approximately 43%, 40% and 32% of our total product
sales for the fiscal years ended June 30, 2006, 2005 and 2004.&#160; One of these distributors, Compex
Technologies (formerly Rehabilicare, Inc.) was our second largest distributor
and accounted for over 16% of our total product sales during each of the past
three fiscal years.&#160; Following their
acquisition by Encore Medical Corporation, the parent company of our primary
competitor (Empi, Inc.), Compex elected to terminate its distribution agreement
with us effective July 1, 2006.&#160; The loss
of this distributor will have a negative effect on our future sales and
operating results.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#160;<b><i style="font-weight:bold;">Demand for our products is
dependent on third party reimbursement.</i></b></font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Product sales
depend, in part, on continued reimbursement by third party payers to clinicians
and their patients for using our products in patient treatments.&#160; These third party payers, including
government health administration authorities, private health insurers and other
organizations, can affect the pricing and relative attractiveness of using our
products and competing products, including alternative therapies, by regulating
reimbursement levels.&#160; Changes in these
relative reimbursement levels may affect sales of our product.&#160; In addition, some of these payers limit
reimbursement amounts paid to health care providers for use of our products in
certain applications and may further limit reimbursement in the future.&#160; Furthermore, significant uncertainty exists
as to the reimbursement status of any new product we may develop.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">The
business in which we operate is intensely competitive and prone to rapid
technological change.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our commercial
business has formidable competition, and we expect competition to remain
intense during fiscal 2007 and beyond.&#160;
Our technology competes with various companies in the drug delivery,
pharmaceutical and biotechnology industries.&#160;
These industries are highly competitive and rapidly evolving with
significant developments expected to continue at a rapid pace.&#160;&#160; Our competitors include public and private
corporations, academic institutions, governmental agencies and public and
private research organizations that are involved in developing, manufacturing
or marketing iontophoretic and other drug delivery systems.&#160; Many of our competitors are substantially
larger with greater financial and other resources, have more experience, have
greater name recognition, offer broader product lines, and are able to offer
discounts as a competitive tactic.&#160; Our
competitors may succeed in more rapidly developing competing technologies,
obtaining FDA approval, or gaining market share for products than us.&#160; Many competitors currently have drug delivery
products approved or in development.&#160; Some
of these products could be more effective or commercially attractive to our
customers than our products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the case of new
products, the first product to reach the market is often able to establish and
maintain significant market share relative to later entrants to the
market.&#160; New drugs or further development
of alternative drug delivery methods may provide greater therapeutic benefits
for a specific drug or indication or may offer comparable performance at lower
costs than our products.&#160;&#160; Our competitors&#146;
ability to more rapidly develop new products than us represents a significant
competitive advantage.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">A

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our success

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The patent

may not result in issued patents, we or our licensors may not protect issued
patents, we may become involved in patent infringement actions, and our and our
licensor&#146;s patents may not be enforceable or may not provide meaningful
protection.&#160; We also operate in many
foreign countries that do not protect intellectual property rights to the same

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We also rely on

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Product

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">It is very

trials that demonstrate our products are both safe and effective for use in the
target indications.&#160; The results of

large scale testing.&#160; A new product could
also produce undesirable side effects that could result in the interruption,

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If our future

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">The
regulation of our business is extensive and uncertain.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In the United
States, the research, development, manufacture and marketing of our products is
regulated by the FDA, which requires approval of drugs and medical devices
before they can be marketed.&#160; Similar
approvals are also required from other regulatory bodies outside the United
States.&#160; The regulatory processes
established by these government agencies are extensive and uncertain, and
compliance is expensive.&#160; In addition, an
approval may be withdrawn and the applicable regulations may change.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Even if we obtain
and maintain regulatory approval for a product, the manufacture of it and
related operations are subject to extensive government regulation and periodic
inspections to confirm compliance with procedures relative to control and
documentation of product design, control and validation of the manufacturing
process and overall product quality.&#160;
Discovery of a failure to comply with applicable regulations could
result in FDA or other regulatory sanctions, restrictions, or an order to
withdraw and/or recall a product.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The FDA currently
allows us to market our iontophoretic dose controllers and electrode products
for use with ions of soluble salts or other drugs under the FDA&#146;s 510(k)
regulations governing medical devices.&#160;
We also have FDA approval to market Iontocaine, our own brand of
lidocaine, for use with our Phoresor system but stopped marketing Iontocaine in
fiscal 2005.&#160; In 1994, the FDA publicly
stated that it intends to require manufacturers of iontophoretic devices to
obtain Pre-Market Approval (PMA) for marketed devices currently used with drugs
not specifically labeled for iontophoretic delivery, which would include our
dose controller for use with ions of soluble salts or other drugs, such as
dexamethasone.&#160; The agency to date has
not published such a regulation.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">If the FDA
requires a PMA for our iontophoretic devices, we would be required to seek FDA
approval to continue to market those devices.&#160;
Such a regulation could require that an application be filed as quickly
as 90 days after the publication date of the regulation.&#160; In such an event we might not be able to
complete and file a PMA within the prescribed time period, or the FDA might not
provide approval.&#160; Failure to submit a
PMA within the prescribed time period and ultimately to obtain FDA approval
could result in our being required to cease commercial distribution of the
Phoresor system for use with dexamethasone or any other drug other than
Iontocaine.&#160; Any interference with our
ability to distribute our Phoresor system for use with dexamethasone would have
a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our iontophoretic
dose controller and electrode kits are marketed under 510(k) clearance.&#160; Since obtaining these clearances we have made
modifications to certain products.&#160; Under
the FDA&#146;s regulations, we are required to obtain an additional 510(k) clearance
if we modify a device for which we have previously received a 510(k) clearance
in a way that significantly affects the safety or efficacy of the device, or if
the modification results in a major change in intended use.&#160; Based on the limited guidance provided by the
FDA to assist manufacturers in determining whether they are required to obtain
a 510(k) clearance for a modified device, we determined that a new 510(k)
submission was not required in connection with certain products.&#160; However, the FDA could require us to obtain
one or more additional 510(k) clearances in the future for certain of those
products.&#160; During that process, we could
be prohibited from marketing the modified device until the clearance is
obtained from the FDA.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">We
may require additional capital in the future and that capital may not be
available.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our future capital
requirements depend on many factors, including:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the costs,
timing, and success of our product development activities, including
preclinical studies and clinical trials and the terms of any associated
collaborative relationship;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>market demand
for any new product resulting from our product development activity;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>requirements to
improve or increase manufacturing capacity;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the costs,
timing, and success of our sales and marketing efforts</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>acquisition
opportunities;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the terms of any
new collaborative relationships;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>competing
technological and market developments; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>the
costs to obtain, maintain and to enforce our intellectual property rights and
defend ourselves from claims that we have infringed a third party&#146;s
intellectual property rights.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">19</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Although we
believe that at current operating levels, existing cash balances and cash
generated from operations will be sufficient to fund our operating needs
through fiscal 2008 and beyond; we may be required or elect to raise additional
capital before that time.&#160; To satisfy
capital requirements, we may seek to raise funds through public or private
financings, collaborative relationships or other arrangements that may be
dilutive to shareholders, involve significant restrictive covenants, or require
us to relinquish rights to certain technologies, products or marketing
territories.&#160; Additional capital, if
required, may not be available on terms satisfactory to us, if at all.&#160; Failure to raise capital when needed could
have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results
of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Acquisition
activity could disrupt our ongoing business and involve significant risks.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Acquisitions are
inherently risky.&#160; We can not be certain
that an acquisition will be successful and will not materially adversely affect
our business.&#160; We have acquired and in
the future may evaluate and acquire businesses, services, products or
technologies that compliment our strategic direction.&#160; These acquisitions may involve significant
risks, including:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>potentially
dilutive issuances of our stock;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>incurrence of
debt and contingent liabilities;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>inability to
successfully integrate the acquired technologies, services, products, and
operations into our business and to maintain uniform standards, controls,
policies and procedures;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>distraction of
management from normal business operations;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>insufficient
revenue generation to offset liabilities assumed and justify the purchase
price;</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>write offs related
to intangible assets; and</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 18.0pt;text-indent:-18.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Symbol" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&#183;</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>unidentified
issues not discovered in the due diligence process.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Product
liability insurance is costly and difficult to obtain.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Product liability
insurance in our industry is expensive and difficult to obtain and we may not
be able to maintain existing levels of coverage or obtain desired coverage on
acceptable terms in the future.&#160;&#160; In
addition, we are not sure if our existing coverage is adequate.&#160; An inability to maintain or obtain sufficient
product liability insurance on acceptable terms to protect against potential
product liability claims could prevent or inhibit the continued
commercialization of our products.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">If we
were successfully sued for product liability we could face substantial
liabilities.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our business
exposes us to potential liability risks inherent in the testing, marketing and
sale of drug delivery and related pharmaceutical products for use in humans,
including product liability claims, product recall, or excessive warranty
claims. The use of our products in clinical trials and the sale of future
products may also expose us to potential product liability risks.&#160; A successful product liability claim in
excess of our insurance coverage could have a material adverse effect on our
business and could further prevent us from obtaining product liability
insurance in the future on commercially desirable or reasonable terms.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">Our
business involves environmental risks that may result in liability for us.</font></i></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our research and
development activities involve the controlled use of hazardous materials,
chemicals and various radioactive compounds.&#160;
The use, disposal and handling of these materials are extensively
regulated by federal, state and local government authorities.&#160; Although we believe our safety procedures for
handling and disposing of such materials comply in all material respects with
the standards prescribed by state and federal regulations, the risk of
accidental environmental contamination or personal injury from these materials
cannot be completely eliminated and we could be required to incur significant
costs to comply with applicable regulations in the future.&#160; Furthermore, in the event of an accident, we
could be held liable for any damages and any such liability could exceed our
resources.</font></p>

STAFF COMMENTS</b><a name="Item1b_UnresolvedStaffComments_155237"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Not applicable.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-60.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 2.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>PROPERTIES</b><a name="Item2_Properties_155309"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Our administrative, manufacturing operations, and research office space
is housed in a single facility, consisting of approximately 34,000 square feet,
located at 2441 South 3850 West in Salt Lake City, Utah.&#160; The facility is leased to us until December
31, 2012.&#160; We believe our facilities will
be adequate and suitable for our present needs and that additional space will
be available as needed.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-60.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 3.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>LEGAL
PROCEEDINGS</b><a name="Item3_LegalProceedings_155307"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The following
discussion provides a summary of certain outstanding and settled legal
matters.&#160; In addition to the specific
legal matters discussed below, we are subject to various claims and legal
proceedings covering matters that arise in the ordinary course of business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">(a)
Outstanding Legal Matters</font></u></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;font-weight:bold;">EEMSO,
Inc. v. Compex Technologies, Inc. f/k/a Rehabilicare, Inc. (&#147;Compex&#148;) and
Iomed, Inc.</font></i>,</b> U.S. District Court for the Northern
District of Texas<i>.</i>&#160;
This action was initially filed on April 6, 2005 by a competitor of
Iomed in the District Court of Dallas County, Texas, 192<font size="1" style="font-size:6.5pt;position:relative;top:-3.0pt;">nd</font>&#160;Judicial District and was removed by Iomed and
co-defendant Compex Technologies to the U.S. District for the Northern District
of Texas, Dallas Division.&#160; The complaint
alleges that Compex, a distributor of Iomed&#146;s iontophoretic drug delivery
products, wrongfully and in violation of a non-disclosure agreement with EEMSO,
provided confidential proprietary information to Iomed pertaining to an
integrated electrode iontophoretic device that had been developed by EEMSO.&#160; The complaint further alleges that Iomed
misappropriated this information and incorporated features of the EEMSO product
in its own integrated electrode product (the Companion 80), and that Iomed is
liable for interference with contract, unfair competition, conversion and civil
conspiracy.&#160; EEMSO seeks injunctive
relief and unspecified monetary damages.&#160;
The case is scheduled for trial in October 2006.&#160; The Company believes that EEMSO&#146;s claims are
without merit and will continue a vigorous defense.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management does not believe that the outcomes of the
legal matters discussed in this section above will have a material adverse
impact on the Company.&#160; However, the
legal fees and expenses in these actions will likely be substantial and, in the
event of an unfavorable resolution, the outcome could have a material adverse
impact on our business, financial position, or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">(b)
Settled Legal Matters</font></u></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective August
31, 2005, we entered into a settlement that resolved our involvement in all
legal matters related to two civil complaints we filed in April 2002 in state
court against two former executives, among others, alleging misappropriation of
our trade secrets, interference with economic relationships and civil
conspiracy.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective January
24, 2006, we entered into a settlement agreement with Travanti Pharma, Inc.
(the successor to Birch Point Medical, Inc.) with respect to the action brought
against us by Birch Point Medical.&#160;
Pursuant to the settlement agreement, we acquired a fully paid-up,
non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license and a perpetual covenant not to
sue under certain patents and patents pending belonging to Travanti Pharma,
Inc. with respect to our iontophoretic medical device products sold into the
orthopedic therapy market for a one-time license fee of $750,000.&#160; The settlement agreement also provided for a
mutual release of claims.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-60.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 4.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>SUBMISSION
OF MATTERS TO A VOTE OF SECURITY HOLDERS</b><a name="Item4_SubmissionOfMattersToAVoteO_155319"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">No matters were
submitted to a vote of security holders during the fourth quarter of the fiscal
year covered by this Report.</font></p>

<h3 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:auto;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Dividends</font></b></h3>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have not paid
dividends to date and do not anticipate or contemplate paying cash dividends in
the foreseeable future.&#160; It is the present
intention of management to utilize all available funds for the development and
growth of our business.</font></p>

$1.0 million, $0.4 million, and $0.4 million in fiscal years 2006, 2005, 2004,
and 2003, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 15.0pt;text-indent:-15.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(2)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reflects the reversal of the remaining accrual amount
relating to the fiscal 2000 lease abandonment charge for facilities relocation.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 15.0pt;text-indent:-15.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(3)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Reflects a $1,190,000 non-recurring, non-cash charge
for the impairment of long-lived assets and a $505,000 non-recurring
restructuring charge.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 15.0pt;text-indent:-15.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(4)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Includes income from contract research, royalties, and
license fees.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt 15.0pt;text-indent:-15.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(5)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As a result of adopting Financial Accounting Standards
Board Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 123R, fiscal 2006 net
income includes a non-cash charge of $150,000 related to stock-based compensation
expense.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 15.0pt;text-indent:-15.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(6)</font><font size="1" style="font-size:3.0pt;">&#160;&#160;&#160; </font><font size="2" style="font-size:10.0pt;">See Notes to Consolidated Financial Statements for
