<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt 60.0pt;text-indent:-60.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Item 7.</font></b><b><font size="1" style="font-size:8.0pt;font-weight:bold;">&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; </font>MANAGEMENT&#146;S
DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS <a name="Item7_ManagementsDiscussionAndAna_155439"></a>OF OPERATIONS</b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">The
following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations
should be read in conjunction with the Consolidated Financial Statements and
the related Notes thereto included elsewhere in this Report.&#160; The following Management&#146;s Discussion and
Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations contains
forward-looking statements, within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities
Act of 1933 and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, that
involve risks and uncertainties.&#160; Our
actual results of operations could differ significantly from those anticipated
in such forward-looking statements as a result of numerous factors discussed
under Item 1 &#147;Business&#148; and elsewhere in this Report.</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Overview</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We are a leader in
the development, manufacture and sale of active drug delivery systems primarily
used to treat local inflammation in the physical and occupational therapy and
sports medicine markets.&#160; Our current
product line is based on proprietary iontophoretic drug delivery
technology.&#160; The majority of our revenues
have been generated through the sale of the Phoresor system, including the
reusable dose controller and single use, disposable patch kits.&#160; We are pursuing opportunities to advance our
position as a provider of quality, innovative medical products that improve
patient healthcare.&#160; In addition, we are
seeking collaborative opportunities to develop its non-invasive drug delivery
technology to satisfy unmet medical needs.&#160;
We have proprietary iontophoresis technology in various stages of
research and product development primarily for transdermal drug delivery and
for the treatment of ophthalmic disease.&#160;
From our inception through fiscal 2002, we have generally incurred
operating losses as a result of costs associated with internally funded
research and development activities.&#160;
During fiscal 2003, 2004, 2005 and 2006, we reported net income.&#160; As of June 30, 2006, our accumulated deficit
was approximately $31.1 million.&#160; Our
ability to sustain profitability will depend on our ability to achieve market
acceptance and successfully expand sales of our existing products and
successfully complete the development of, receive regulatory approvals for, and
successfully manufacture and market our current and future products, and
resolve pending litigation matters, as to which there can be no assurance.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Strategic Assessment Update</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">On
September 15, 2005, we announced that our Board of Directors decided to explore
various strategic alternatives for the Company to maximize shareholder
value.&#160; In connection with this process,
we retained Seven Hills Partners LLC to act as our financial advisor.&#160; We have engaged in discussions with various
parties regarding potential transactions.&#160;
At the present time, the assessment of strategic alternatives is
ongoing.&#160; We are uncertain whether any
transaction will result from this process and if a transaction does result from
that process what form it will take and what impact it may have on our stock
price.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Loss of Distributor</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We were party to a
distribution agreement with Compex Technologies, Inc. (formerly Rehabilicare,
Inc.) that was terminated effective July 1, 2006.&#160;&#160; Compex was our second largest customer and
accounted for over 16% of our total product sales during each of the past three
fiscal years.&#160; Compex elected to
terminate the Distribution Agreement (the &#147;Agreement&#148;) between Iomed, Inc. and
Rehabilicare following their acquisition by Encore Medical Corporation, the
parent company of our primary competitor, Empi, Inc.&#160; These events will likely have a negative
effect on our future sales and operating results.&#160; Nevertheless, we believe that user
preference, the strength of our alternative distribution channels and our own
internal sales and marketing efforts provide us with an opportunity to retain a
substantial portion of the revenue generated by the end user customers formerly
serviced by Compex.&#160; The Agreement
provided us with certain provisions to protect our business interests following
such termination.&#160; Under the Agreement,
Compex is subject to a twelve month non-compete provision and we were provided
access to end user customer data.&#160; We
intend to exercise our rights under the Agreement and to utilize alternative
distribution channels to service former Compex accounts.&#160; Due to certain factors, including various
market dynamics, limited resources, and our limited access to the end user
account information of our distributors; it will be difficult for the Company
to precisely measure its success in retaining these accounts.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fiscal Years Ended June 30, 2006
and 2005</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Product
sales.&#160; </font></i>Product sales
decreased 5% to $10.8 million in fiscal 2006 from $11.4 million in fiscal 2005
primarily due to reduced unit sales volume to large dealers, including Compex
Technologies, during the fourth quarter of fiscal 2006.&#160; In addition, a slight decrease in average
selling prices during the first quarter of fiscal 2006 compared with the first
quarter of fiscal 2005 contributed to lower sales in fiscal 2006.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Costs of Products Sold.&#160; </font></i>Costs of products sold were
$4.3 million in fiscal 2006 compared to $4.4 million in the prior year.&#160; Gross margins on product sales were 60.6% in
fiscal 2006 compared to 61.5% in the prior year.&#160; Improved material costs, labor efficiencies
and overhead costs partially mitigated the effects of lower total unit sales
volume on gross margin.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Selling, General and Administrative Expenses.&#160; </font></i>Selling, general and
administrative expenses decreased 9% to $5.2 million in fiscal 2006 compared to
$5.7 million in the prior year.&#160; The decrease
relates primarily to reduced personnel, professional fees and
litigation-related expenses (See &#147;Item 3. Legal Proceedings&#148;).&#160;&#160; Expenses related to litigation were $0.9
million and $1.0 million in fiscal 2006 and 2005, respectively.&#160;&#160; We continue to look for opportunities to
reduce expenses.&#160; The beneficial effects
of a re-negotiated facility lease also resulted in additional expense
reductions and cash flow contributions during fiscal 2006.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Research and Product Development
Expense.&#160; </font></i>Research and
product development expenditures increased 11% to $1.1 million in fiscal 2006
compared to $1.0 million for the prior year.&#160;
The increase is a result of increased investment in new product
development activities for our core business offset, in part, by the beneficial
effects of the renegotiated facility lease, including decreased allocations of
monthly rent and depreciation expense.&#160;
During fiscal 2007, we intend to focus research and product development
efforts on our core business and new market opportunities for our iontophoresis
technology.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other Income and Expenses.&#160; </font></i>&#160;Interest expense decreased to $78,000 in
fiscal 2006 from $121,000 in the prior year due to a decreasing balance on
long-term obligations.&#160; Interest income
and other miscellaneous income was $384,000 in fiscal 2006 compared to $217,000
in the prior year.&#160; Amounts in both
periods primarily reflect interest earnings on invested cash balances and
income from a royalty and license agreement.&#160;
The increase was due to increased interest income from improved rates.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes.&#160; </font></i>During fiscal years 2006
and 2005, we recognized no income tax expense due to certain future tax
benefits and the reversal of valuation allowance that had been previously
recorded to offset deferred tax assets associated with our net operating loss
carryforwards.&#160; We have substantial net
operating loss carryforwards, which, under the current &#147;change of ownership&#148;
rules of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, may become subject to
substantial annual limitation in the future.&#160;
Such &#147;changes of ownership&#148; can result from purchases and sales of our
shares by large shareholders.&#160; If we
experience a 50% change in the ownership of our stock, then we may be limited
in the amount of net operating loss carryforwards that we can use in any given
year.&#160; Due to the uncertainty of the
realizability of our net deferred tax assets, primarily associated with net
operating loss carryforwards, we have recorded a full valuation allowance to
offset these deferred tax assets.&#160; We
will continue to monitor the realizability of these assets and could adjust the
valuation allowance in the future.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Net Income.&#160; </font></i>We recognized net income of
$600,000, or $0.08 per diluted share, during fiscal 2006 compared with net
income of $425,000, or $0.06 per diluted share, during the prior year. Net
income in the current year was negatively affected by a non-cash charge of
$150,000 for stock option compensation expense following the Company&#146;s adoption
of FASB Statement No. 123R, Share-Based Payment.&#160; The increase in net income is a result of the
various factors discussed above.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Fiscal Years Ended June 30, 2005
and 2004</font></b></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Product sales.&#160; </font></i>Product sales were $11.4
million in fiscal 2005, a 6% decrease from $12.2 million in fiscal 2004.&#160; Product sales in fiscal 2005 were impacted by
a reduction in average selling prices due, in part, to factors relating to the
restructuring of our distribution network.&#160;
In addition, the effect of cost constraints in physical therapy clinics,
including legislative changes in certain workers&#146; compensation markets, is,
among other factors, resulting in decreased reimbursement for physical therapy
services, which may have an indirect impact on the utilization of our
products.&#160; Other market trends resulted in
an increasing portion of our sales to large national suppliers who offer a
broader line of products and lower overall pricing.&#160; These</p>

The beneficial effects of the renegotiated facility lease, beginning in

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Selling, General and Administrative Expenses.&#160; </font></i>Selling, general and
administrative expenses increased 2% to $5.7 million in fiscal 2005 compared to
$5.6 million in fiscal 2004.&#160; The
increase relates primarily to litigation expenses which off-set the reductions
in on-going selling, general and administrative expenses achieved from
operating efficiencies initiated over the last four years.&#160; Expenses related to litigation, including the
establishment of reserves with respect thereto, were $1.0 million and $0.4
million in fiscal 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160;&#160;
We continue to look for opportunities to reduce expenses.&#160; The beneficial effects of a re-negotiated
facility lease also resulted in additional expense reductions and cash flow
contributions during fiscal 2005.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Research and Product Development
Expense.&#160; </font></i>Research and
product development expenditures decreased 5% to $1.0 million in fiscal 2005
compared to $1.1 million for fiscal 2004.&#160;
The decrease is primarily a result of the beneficial effects of the
renegotiated facility lease, including decreased allocations of monthly rent
and depreciation expense.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Other Income and Expenses.&#160; </font></i>&#160;Interest expense decreased to $121,000 in
fiscal 2005 from $169,000 in fiscal 2004 due to a decreasing balance on
long-term obligations.&#160; Interest income
and other miscellaneous income was $217,000 in fiscal 2005 compared to $184,000
in fiscal 2004.&#160; Amounts in both periods
reflect interest earnings on invested cash balances and income from a royalty
and license agreement.&#160; The increase was
due to increased interest income from improved rates and a larger invested cash
balance offset, in part, by reduced royalty income from the royalty and license
agreement.&#160; Under the terms of this
agreement, the royalty rate decreased beginning during fiscal 2004.</p>

<p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></i><font face="Times New Roman">.&#160; No income tax expense was recognized for fiscal 2005 or 2004.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Net Income.&#160; </font></i>We recognized net income of

income of $954,000, or $0.12 per diluted share, during fiscal 2004.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal 2006, 2005,
and 2004, our operations, including costs associated with its research and

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of June 30, 2006, we had

million of long-term restricted cash, invested in mutual funds and used to
secure long-term financing.&#160; Cash in
excess of immediate requirements is invested in a manner which is intended to
maximize liquidity and return while minimizing investment risk, and, whenever
possible, we seek to minimize the potential effects of concentration of credit
risk.</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">We

activities in fiscal 2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; The decrease in positive operating cash flow
in fiscal 2006 was a result of </font>a net decrease in trade accounts payable
and accrued expenses related to the timing of payments for litigation and other
expenses.&#160; </font>&#160;In fiscal 2005, the decrease in
cash generated from operations was primarily related to the reduced net income
and depreciation partially offset by the timing of payments for certain accrued
litigation expenses and other liabilities.</p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of June 30, 2006, we
had approximately $0.8 million in debt, including the current portion,
outstanding under financing agreements.&#160;
We do not anticipate a significant investment in capital equipment
during the next 12 months.&#160; Our equipment
and furniture expenditures were $60,000, $61,000, and $95,000 in fiscal</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">Critical Accounting Policies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Securities Exchange Commission&#146;s Financial Reporting Release No. 60 requires
all companies to include a discussion of critical accounting policies or
methods used in the preparation of financial statements.&#160; The following list is not intended to be a
comprehensive list of all of our accounting policies.&#160; Our significant accounting policies are more
fully described in Note 1 of our consolidated financial statements.&#160; In many cases, the accounting treatment of a
particular transaction is dictated by U.S. generally accepted accounting
principles, with no need for management&#146;s judgment or estimation in
application.&#160; There are also areas in
which management&#146;s judgment in selecting an available alternative would not
produce a materially different result.&#160;
The following is a brief discussion of the more significant accounting
policies and methods we employ:</font></p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">General</font></i> - The preparation of financial statements in conformity with U.S.
generally accepted accounting principles requires management to make estimates
and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities at
the date of the financial statements and the reported amounts of revenues and
expenses during the reporting period.&#160;
Actual results could differ from those estimates.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font></i> &#150; Revenues on product sales are recognized when there is persuasive
evidence that an arms length transfer has occurred, generally upon shipment,
when title has passed, and the price is fixed or determinable.&#160; We provide our customers certain purchase
incentives, including performance rebates and volume pricing discounts, based
on the achievement of specified purchase levels.&#160; We accrue for performance rebates based upon
estimated customer purchase levels and records volume pricing discounts when
products are purchased.&#160; Revenue, which
is stated as net product sales, is reduced by these incentives.</p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">27</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Long Lived Assets</font></i> &#150; The carrying amounts of long-lived assets, and the related
amortization periods, are reviewed for impairment whenever events occur or
changes in circumstances indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not
be recoverable within the estimated useful life.&#160; When we determine the existence of impairment
indicators, the impairment loss is measured based on the excess of carrying
value over the estimated fair value of the impaired assets.&#160; The carrying value of the underlying assets
is reduced, with the reduction charged to expense, so that the carrying value
is equal to estimated fair value.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Inventories</font></i> &#150; Inventories are stated at the lower of cost or market.&#160; Cost is determined using the first-in,
first-out method.&#160; We evaluate the
carrying value of its inventories at least quarterly, taking into account such
factors as historical and anticipated future sales compared with quantities on
hand, the price we expect to obtain for its products in their respective
markets compared with historical cost, and the remaining shelf life of goods on
hand.</p>

<p style="font-family:Times New Roman;font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock-based
Compensation</font></i> &#150; We
have adopted Financial Accounting Standards Board Statement of Financial
Accounting Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No. 123R, Share-Based Payment.&#160; We use the Modified Prospective method, which
requires the application of SFAS No. 123R to new awards and to awards modified,
repurchased or cancelled after the effective date.&#160; Additionally, compensation cost for the
portion of outstanding awards for which service has not been rendered (such as
unvested options) that are outstanding as of the date of adoption will be
recognized as the remaining services are rendered.&#160; We recorded $150,000 in stock-based
compensation expense during the fiscal 2006.&#160;
Results from prior periods have not been restated.</p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">REPORT OF
INDEPENDENT REGISTERED PUBLIC ACCOUNTING FIRM</font></b><a name="ReportOfIndependentRegisteredPubl_143751"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Board of Directors and Shareholders</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">IOMED, Inc.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We have audited the
accompanying balance sheets of IOMED, Inc. as of June 30, 2006 and 2005, and
the related statements of income, shareholders&#146; equity, and cash flows for each
of the three years in the period ended June 30, 2006. These financial
statements are the responsibility of the Company&#146;s management. Our
responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on
our audits.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">We conducted our audits
in accordance with the standards of the Public Company Accounting Oversight
Board (United States). Those standards require that we plan and perform the
audit to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are
free of material misstatement. We were not engaged to perform an audit of the
Company&#146;s internal control over financial reporting. Our audits included
consideration of internal control over financial reporting as a basis for
designing audit procedures that are appropriate in the circumstances, but not
for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the Company&#146;s
internal control over financial reporting.&#160;
Accordingly, we express no such opinion. An audit also includes
examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting the amounts and disclosures in
the financial statements, assessing the accounting principles used and
significant estimates made by management, and evaluating the overall financial
statement presentation.&#160; We believe that
our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In our opinion, the
financial statements referred to above present fairly, in all material
respects, the financial position of IOMED, Inc. at June 30, 2006 and 2005, and
the results of its operations and its cash flows for each of the three years in
the period ended June 30, 2006, in conformity with U.S. generally accepted
accounting principles.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As discussed in Notes 1
and 5 to the financial statements, effective July 1, 2005, the Company adopted
Statement of Financial Accounting Standards No. 123 (revised 2004), &#147;Share
Based Payment.&#148;</font></p>

<p align="center" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:center;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">NOTES TO FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</font></b><a name="NotesToFinancialStatements_161035"></a></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">1.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Description of Business and Summary of Significant
Accounting Policies</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Description of Business</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">IOMED, Inc., a Utah
corporation (the &#147;Company&#148;), is a leader in the development, manufacture and
sale of active drug delivery systems used primarily to treat acute local
inflammation in the physical and occupational therapy and sports medicine
markets.&#160; The Company is pursuing
opportunities to advance its position as a provider of quality, innovative
medical products that improve patient healthcare.&#160; In addition, the Company is seeking
collaborative opportunities to develop its non-invasive drug delivery
technology to satisfy unmet medical needs.&#160;
The Company has proprietary technology in various stages of research and
product development primarily for transdermal drug delivery and for the
treatment of ophthalmic disease.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Estimates</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Preparation of financial
statements in conformity with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles
requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported
amounts of assets and liabilities at the date of the financial statements and
the reported amounts of revenue and expenses during the reporting period.&#160; Actual results could differ from those
estimates.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Cash Equivalents</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
Company considers all highly liquid investments with maturities of three months
or less, when purchased, to be cash equivalents, including $310,000 restricted
to secure the current portion of certain long-term obligations (see note 4).</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Concentrations of Credit Risk</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company&#146;s financial
instruments that are exposed to concentrations of credit risk consist primarily
of cash, cash equivalents and trade accounts receivable.&#160; Cash and cash equivalents are held in
federally insured financial institutions or invested in high-grade short-term
commercial paper issued by major United States corporations.&#160; The Company sells its products primarily to,
and has trade accounts receivable with, independent durable medical equipment
dealers in the United States and abroad.&#160;
Less than 10% of product sales are to foreign customers.&#160; As a general policy, collateral is not
required for accounts receivable.&#160; The
Company maintains an allowance for losses based upon expected collections of
accounts receivable.&#160; Additionally,
customers&#146; financial condition and credit worthiness are regularly evaluated
and historical losses have not been material.&#160;
Combined sales to the Company&#146;s two largest customers accounted for
approximately 43%, 40% and 32% of the Company&#146;s total product sales for the
years ended June 30, 2006, 2005 and 2004.&#160;
At June 30, 2006, 2005 and 2004, amounts due from such customers
accounted for approximately 56%, 55% and 47% of trade receivables, all of which
was current.&#160; Effective July 1, 2006, the
distribution agreement between the Company and one of these customers has
terminated.&#160; The Company is evaluating
the impact on future operations.&#160; The
Company considers credit risk from concentrations of trade accounts receivable
to be low.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Revenue Recognition</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Revenues on product sales are recognized when there is persuasive
evidence that an arms length transfer has occurred, generally upon shipment,
when title has passed, the price is fixed or determinable, and collectibility
is reasonably assured.&#160; The Company
provides its customers certain purchase incentives, including performance
rebates and volume pricing discounts, based on the achievement of specified
purchase levels.&#160; The Company accrues for
performance rebates based upon estimated customer purchase levels and records
volume pricing discounts when products are purchased.&#160; Revenue,
which is stated as net product sales, is reduced by these incentives.</font></p>

<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Research and Product Development
and Patent Costs</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company expenses
costs associated with its research and development efforts, including
collaborative relationship efforts, as incurred.&#160; Research and development expenses include
salaries and benefits, facility costs, overhead allocations, clinical trials,
consulting, contract services, and costs related to development of commercial
scale manufacturing capabilities.&#160; The
Company also incurs certain costs in the preparation, application, filing,
maintenance and defense of patents and trademarks.&#160; Where such costs primarily relate to patents
and trademarks covering technologies or products which are under development or
in the early stages of commercialization, the Company expenses such costs as
incurred.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Inventories</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman"><font style="font-size:10.0pt;">Inventories
are stated at the lower of cost or market.&#160;
Cost is determined using the first-in, first-out method.&#160; The Company evaluates the carrying value of
its inventories at least quarterly, taking into account such factors as
historical and anticipated future sales compared with quantities on hand, the
price the Company expects to obtain for its products in their respective
markets compared with historical cost, and the remaining shelf life of goods on
hand.</font>&#160; Inventories consist of the
following:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Long Lived Assets</font></i></h2>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The
carrying amounts of long-lived assets, and the related amortization periods,
are reviewed for impairment whenever events occur or changes in circumstances
indicate that the carrying amount of an asset may not be recoverable within the
estimated useful life.&#160; When the Company
determines the existence of impairment indicators, the impairment loss is
measured based on the excess of carrying value over the estimated fair value of
the impaired assets. &#160;The carrying value
of the underlying asset is reduced, with the reduction charged to operating
expense, so that the carrying amount is equal to the estimated fair value.</font></p>


 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">37</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='37',FILE='C:\fc\270173156981_D10695_1386791\20304-1-fg.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Sep 27 17:32 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>


<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Stock-based Compensation</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company adopted
Financial Accounting Standards Board Statement of Financial Accounting
Standards (&#147;SFAS&#148;) No. 123R, Share-Based Payment, effective as of July 1, 2005,
the beginning of the Company&#146;s fiscal year.&#160;
The Company has adopted the Modified Prospective method, which requires
the application of SFAS No. 123R to new awards and to awards modified,
repurchased or cancelled after the effective date.&#160; Additionally, compensation cost for the
portion of outstanding awards for which service has not been rendered (such as
unvested options) that are outstanding as of the date of adoption will be
recognized as the remaining services are rendered.&#160; Results from prior periods have not been
restated.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Through June 30, 2005,
the Company elected to follow Accounting Principles Board Opinion No. 25 - <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock Issued to Employees</font></i>
(APB 25) and related interpretations in accounting for its employee stock
options rather than adopting the alternative fair value accounting provided for
under SFAS No. 123, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for
Stock-Based Compensation</font></i>, as amended by SFAS No. 148, <i><font style="font-style:italic;">Accounting for Stock Based Compensation &#150; Transition
and Disclosure</font></i>, and as a result the Company did not recognize any
compensation expense.&#160; The table below
illustrates the effect on net income and income per share had compensation cost
for the Company&#146;s employee stock options been determined consistent with the
fair value methodology prescribed under SFAS 123 for the fiscal years ended
June 30, 2005 and 2004.&#160; Net income for
the fiscal year ended June 30, 2006 includes $150,000 in stock-based compensation
expense.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The fair value of stock
option grants were determined using the Black-Scholes option valuation model,
which was developed for use in estimating the fair value of traded options that
have no vesting restrictions and are fully transferable.&#160; In addition, option valuation models require
the input of highly subjective assumptions, including the expected stock price
volatility.&#160; In management&#146;s opinion the
existing models do not necessarily provide a reliable single measure of the
fair value of its employee stock options because the Company&#146;s employee stock
options have characteristics different from those of traded options and because
changes in the highly subjective input assumptions can materially affect the
fair value estimate.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">In all periods presented,
certain securities were not included in the computation of diluted income per
share due to their antidilutive effect.&#160;
At June 30, 2006, options to purchase approximately 200,000 common
shares at a weighted average exercise price of $4.88 were not included.&#160; At June 30, 2005, options to purchase
approximately 669,000 common shares were not included.&#160; At June 30, 2004, options to purchase
approximately 422,000 common shares were not included.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Income Taxes</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company accounts for
income taxes using the asset and liability method.&#160; Under the asset and liability method,
deferred tax assets and liabilities are recognized for the future tax
consequences attributable to differences between the financial statement
carrying amounts of existing assets and liabilities and their respective tax
bases, and operating loss and tax credit carryforwards.&#160; Deferred tax assets and liabilities are
measured using enacted tax rates expected to apply to taxable income in the
years in which those temporary differences are expected to be recovered or
settled.&#160; The effect on deferred tax
assets and liabilities of a change in tax rates is recognized in income in the
period that includes the enactment date.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Intangible
Assets</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">At June 30, 2006,
intangible assets totaling $709,000, net of accumulated amortization totaling
$41,000, are included in other assets.&#160;
The intangible assets consist of a fully paid-up, non-exclusive,
worldwide, royalty-free license and other rights under certain issued and
pending patents.&#160; The Company purchased
these assets in fiscal 2006 for $750,000.&#160;
The assets are being amortized on a straight-line basis over an
estimated useful life of seventeen years.&#160;
Amortization expense of $41,000 associated with these assets was
recorded during fiscal 2006.&#160;
Amortization expense for each of the next five years is expected to be
approximately $45,000 per year.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">2.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Restricted Cash</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company maintains an
interest bearing money market account with a lending bank, $275,000 of which is
being held as a compensating balance under a long-term obligation (see notes 1
and 4) and is restricted as to withdrawal.&#160;
The restricted cash balance requirement decreases over the life of the
obligation as payments are made.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">4.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Commitments</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Operating Leases</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company leases
space and certain equipment under non-cancelable operating lease agreements
that expire at various dates through 2012.&#160;
Rental expense for such leases was $277,000, $286,000 and $347,000 for
the years ended June 30, 2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively.&#160; It is generally expected that, in the normal
course of business, operating leases that expire will be renewed or replaced by
other leases with similar terms.&#160; Future
minimum lease payments under non-cancelable operating leases at June 30, 2006,
were $1,856,000.&#160; These obligations mature as follows:&#160; fiscal 2007 &#151; $278,000; fiscal 2008 &#151; $274,000;
fiscal 2009 &#151; $276,000; fiscal 2010 &#151; $283,000; and fiscal 2011 and thereafter
&#151; $745,000.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Long-Term Obligations</font></i></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has acquired
certain equipment and furniture under capital lease agreements.&#160; The capitalized cost of such equipment was
$1,339,000 at June 30, 2006 and 2005 and accumulated amortization was
$1,339,000 and $1,210,000, respectively.&#160;
Under these capital lease agreements, the Company was required to meet
certain financial covenants, all of which were met at all times prior to
conclusion.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During fiscal 2001, the
Company refinanced $2,700,000 of capital lease obligations into a term loan,
collateralized by the underlying assets and restricted cash, with a fixed rate
of 6.82%, payable in 84 monthly installments of $40,519 maturing April 2008.&#160; At June 30, 2006, the outstanding balance was
$836,000.&#160; Payments of approximately
$486,000 are due within one year, of which $443,000 is principal reduction.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-indent:0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The carrying
values of the long-term obligations approximate fair values as the interest
rates on these long-term obligations approximate market rates of interest.&#160; Future minimum payments under long-term
obligations consisted of the following at June 30, 2006:</font></p>

<h2 style="font-weight:normal;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;page-break-after:avoid;"><i><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-style:italic;">Royalty
Agreements</font></i></h2>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is the
licensee under royalty agreements, which provide for the payment of royalties
to the licensor based upon net sales of the products under royalty.&#160; Royalty expense in each of the three years in
the period ended June 30, 2006 was not material.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">5.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Stock-based Compensation</font></b></p><p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has adopted and approved two incentive stock compensation plans.&#160; The Company&#146;s 1988 Stock Option Plan and the 1997 Share Incentive Plan were approved by the shareholders in November 1988 and in November 1997, respectively.&#160; The 1988 Stock Option Plan expired in August 1998 and no further grants were made under the Plan following the adoption of the 1997 Share Incentive Plan.&#160; The Company&#146;s 1997 Share Incentive Plan permits the grant of up to 2,812,500 stock options.&#160; Option awards are generally granted with an exercise price equal to the market price of the of the Company&#146;s stock at the date of grant.&#160; In general, options granted vest over zero to five years and have 10-year contractual terms.&#160; </font><font face="Times New Roman">A summary of activity under the Plans during the fiscal year ended June 30, 2006, 2005, and 2004 is as follows:</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company adopted SFAS No. 123R, Share-Based Payment, effective as of July 1, 2005, the beginning of its fiscal year.&#160; SFAS No. 123R revises SFAS No. 123 and supersedes APB 25 and requires companies to expense the value of employee stock options and other equity-based awards.&#160; For the fiscal year ended June 30, 2006, the Company recorded a total non-cash charge of $150,000 related to stock-based compensation.&#160; As a result of adopting SFAS No. 123R, the Company&#146;s operating income and net income for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2006 were $150,000 less than if the Company had continued to account for stock-based compensation under APB Opinion No. 25.&#160; Basic and diluted net loss per share for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2006 would have increased by $0.02 if the Company had not adopted SFAS No. 123R.</font></p><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company recognizes compensation expense equal to the grant-date fair value of stock-based awards for all awards expected to vest, over the period during which the related service is rendered by grantees. The fair value of stock-based awards is determined primarily using the Black-Scholes pricing model, which is the same valuation model used previously in valuing stock options for the pro forma footnote disclosures under the requirements of SFAS No. 123 (see Note 1).&#160; The Company uses the &#147;straight line&#148; vesting method to value awards and to allocate those values over the requisite service periods, which is the same method as used previously in determining pro forma expense under SFAS No. 123.</font></p>
 <p style="font-size:10.0pt;margin:24.0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"><font face="Times New Roman">41</font></p> <br><hr size="3" width="100%" noshade color="#010101" align="center">

<!-- SEQ.=1,FOLIO='41',FILE='C:\fc\270173156981_D10695_1386791\20304-1-fg.htm',USER='jmsproofassembler',CD='Sep 27 17:32 2006' -->
<br clear="all" style="page-break-before:always;">
 <p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;text-align:center;"></p>
<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Black-Scholes pricing models require using certain assumptions, including expected volatility, dividend yields, risk-free interest rates, expected lives, and forfeiture rates.&#160; Expected stock price volatility, which ranged from 0.47 to 0.75 and had a weighted average of 0.71, was estimated using historical volatilities of the Company&#146;s stock at each grant date.&#160; Expected dividend yields were 0.0%.&#160; US Treasury bill yields with terms corresponding to expected terms of the awards being valued were used to estimate risk-free interest rates, the weighted average of which was 4.2%.&#160; In estimating expected lives, contractual and vesting terms of awards, along with historical experience, were considered; however, due to insufficient historical data from which to reliably estimate expected lives, the Company used estimates based on the &#147;shortcut approach&#148; set forth in SFAS 123R, where the expected life of 6 years was estimated to be the mid-point between the vesting date and the end of the contractual term.&#160; Estimated forfeiture rates were based primarily on historical data.</font></p><p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A summary of activity for non-vested options under the Plans during the period ended June 30, 2006 is as follows:</font></p>

<div align="center">

<table border="0" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="border-collapse:collapse;">
 <tr style="page-break-inside:avoid;">
  <td width="264" valign="bottom" style="padding:0pt .7pt 0pt 0pt;width:198.05pt;">
  <p style="font-size:8.0pt;font-weight:bold;line-height:8.0pt;margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;page-break-after:avoid;text-align:center;"></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The weighted average fair
value of options granted in the years ended June 30, 2006, 2005 and 2004, was
$1.29, $1.46 and $1.45, respectively.&#160;

2006 follows: </font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">6.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Series D Convertible Preferred
Shares</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">During the fiscal
year ended June 30, 2006, all holders of Series D Convertible Preferred Shares
converted their shares into 893,801 shares of common stock on a share for share
basis, pursuant to the terms of such preferred stock.&#160; There are no Series D preferred shares
outstanding at June 30, 2006.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">7.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Employee Benefit Plan</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company has
established a 401(k) savings plan for its full-time employees and makes a
matching contribution based on a percentage of the contributions of
participating employees.&#160; The Company
contributed approximately $99,000, $100,000 and $79,000 for the years ended
June 30, 2006, 2005 and 2004, respectively.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">As of June 30, 2006, the
Company had approximately $19,954,000 and $15,019,000, non tax-effected, in
federal and state net operating loss carryforwards, respectively, and $742,000
in federal tax credit carryforwards, that expire from 2006 through 2025, if not
utilized.&#160; Utilization of the Company&#146;s
net operating loss and tax credit carryforwards is limited to the future
taxable income of the Company.&#160; Under the
&#147;change of ownership&#148; provisions of the Internal Revenue Code, utilization of
these net operating loss and credit carryforwards may be subject to substantial
annual limitation in the future.&#160; Such &#147;changes
of ownership&#148; can result from purchases and sales of our shares by large shareholders.&#160; If such a change in ownership of our shares
was to occur, we may be limited in the amount of net operating loss
carryforwards that we can use in any given year.</font></p>

<p style="font-weight:bold;margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">9.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Contingencies</font></b></p>

<p align="left" style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;text-align:left;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is
subject to various claims and legal proceedings (see Note 11) covering matters
that arise in the ordinary course of its business activities.&#160; Except as otherwise disclosed, management
believes any liability that may ultimately result from the resolution of these
matters will not have a material adverse effect on the Company&#146;s consolidated
financial position, operating results, or cash flows.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt .0001pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">&nbsp;</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><b><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;font-weight:bold;">11.&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160;&#160; Litigation</font></b></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">A description of
certain outstanding and settled legal matters involving the Company is provided
below.&#160; In addition to the legal matters
discussed below, the Company is subject to various claims and legal proceedings
covering matters that arise in the ordinary course of business.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(a) Outstanding Legal
Matters</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">The Company is a
co-defendant with a former distributor of the Company&#146;s products, in a claim
asserting misappropriation of trade secrets.&#160;
The Company has denied all allegations of the complaint.&#160; The case is scheduled for trial in October
2006.&#160; The Company believes that EEMSO&#146;s
claims are without merit and will continue a vigorous defense.&#160; At this stage, it is too early to predict the
outcome.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Management does not
believe that the outcome of this legal matter will have a material adverse
impact on the Company.&#160; However, legal
fees and expenses will likely be substantial and, in the event of an
unfavorable resolution, the outcome could have a material adverse impact on the
Company&#146;s business, financial position, or results of operations.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><u><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">(b) Settled Legal Matters</font></u></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective August 31,
2005, the Company entered into a settlement agreement that resolved the Company&#146;s
involvement in all legal matters related to two civil complaints filed in April
2002 by the Company in state court against two former executives, among others,
alleging misappropriation of the Company&#146;s trade secrets, interference with
economic relationships and civil conspiracy.</font></p>

<p style="margin:0pt 0pt 12.0pt;"><font size="2" face="Times New Roman" style="font-size:10.0pt;">Effective January 24,
2006, the Company entered into a settlement agreement with Travanti Pharma,
Inc. (the successor to Birch Point Medical, Inc.) with respect to the action
brought against the Company by Birch Point Medical.&#160; Pursuant to the settlement agreement, the
Company acquired a fully paid-up, non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free
license and a perpetual covenant not to sue under certain patents and patents
pending belonging to Travanti Pharma, Inc. with respect to the Company&#146;s
iontophoretic medical device products sold into the orthopedic therapy market
for a one-time license fee of $750,000.&#160;
The settlement agreement also provided for a mutual release of claims.</font></p>
